definition: Datasets of prompt + two or more responses with a human (or AI) judgment of which is better.
details: Datasets of prompt + two or more responses with a human (or AI) judgment of which is better. The raw material of reward models and direct preference methods; its quality and diversity bound what alignment can achieve.

explainer.lead: Preference data is prompts paired with two or more responses and a judgment of which is better. It matters because its quality and diversity bound what alignment can achieve.

tiers.eli5: It's like showing someone two drafts of a letter and asking which reads better, then collecting thousands of those answered comparisons.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as the raw material for reward models and direct preference methods. A pitfall is dataset limits: alignment can only be as good and broad as the preference judgments collected.
tiers.paperLevel: Data of the form prompt + two or more responses + a human or AI judgment of which is better; quality and diversity bound alignment outcomes.

explainer.example: A prompt is answered twice, an annotator marks the better response, and the comparison becomes a training item for a reward model.
